In [[mathematics]] &mdash; specifically, in [[measure theory]] &mdash; a '''perfect measure''' (or, more accurately, a '''perfect measure space''') is one that is "[[well-behaved]]" in some sense.  Intuitively, a perfect measure ''&mu;'' is one for which, if we consider the [[pushforward measure]] on the [[real line]] '''R''', then every [[measurable set]] is "''&mu;''-approximately a [[Borel set]]".  The notion of perfectness is closely related to [[tightness of measures]]:  indeed, in [[metric space]]s, tight measures are always perfect.

==Definition==

A [[measure space]] (''X'',&nbsp;&Sigma;,&nbsp;''&mu;'') is said to be '''perfect''' if, for every &Sigma;-measurable function ''f''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''X''&nbsp;→&nbsp;'''R''' and every ''A''&nbsp;&sube;&nbsp;'''R''' with ''f''<sup>&minus;1</sup>(''A'')&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;&Sigma;, there exist Borel subsets ''A''<sub>1</sub> and ''A''<sub>2</sub> of '''R''' such that

:<math>A_{1} \subseteq A \subseteq A_{2} \mbox{ and } \mu \big( f^{-1} ( A_{2} \setminus A_{1} ) \big) = 0.</math>

==Results concerning perfect measures==

* If ''X'' is any metric space and ''&mu;'' is an [[inner regular measure|inner regular]] (or [[tightness of measures|tight]]) measure on ''X'', then (''X'',&nbsp;''B''<sub>''X''</sub>,&nbsp;''&mu;'') is a perfect measure space, where ''B''<sub>''X''</sub> denotes the [[Borel sigma algebra|Borel ''&sigma;''-algebra]] on ''X''.
